verdict.rationale: Lium documents fixed auto-termination settings: a pod is deleted when a chosen TTL, end time or USD spend cap is reached. It also offers a public availability WebSocket that a developer could build automation on. Neither is a user-defined event-to-action rules capability. The termination settings are an adjacent lifecycle control with one preset action, and the WebSocket is a developer building block, so neither earns credit for this story.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events
